thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: service=inference region=us-west-2a symptom=latency_high/5xx spike - paging to #incidents

oncall-eng: got it, picking up. p95 for text-gen up to 1.2s and 5xx rate ~4% across hosted endpoints. Observed from logs: repeated TLS connection resets to nodes in us-west-2a.

sre-aly: seeing node-level network recv errors on g5 pool in 2a. ELB health checks failing for some instances (target unhealthy).

infra-dev: confirming — `kubectl get pods -l svc=inference -o wide` shows several pods stuck Terminating on us-west-2a hosts, ENI flaps reported in /var/log/messages.

netops-tom: AWS NLB metrics show elevated TargetConnectionErrors for 2a, ENI detaches in the AZ at ~04:10 UTC. AWS console shows decreased available capacity in 2a (AZ-specific host networking issue). Filing AWS support case now.

oncall-eng: immediate action: mark us-west-2a as degraded in our router to stop new traffic hitting that AZ. Can infra flip the AZ health flag?

infra-dev: doing that now — running `internal-router set-az-health us-west-2a unhealthy --reason "ENI flaps"`

infra-dev: done. Traffic steering started. Charging flows will failover to 2b/2c. :white_check_mark:

paul: OK steering good, but we still see queued requests for sessions that were pinned to 2a — some are timing out and causing client 5xx. Need session migration/eviction strategy.

maria: we can evict K/V cache entries for those sessions and let them rebuild in new AZs; doing a rolling eviction for the oldest 15m entries now. This should reduce cache-related stalls.

support-liz: getting inbound tickets — some enterprise customers report 5xx and partial feature regressions (streaming cutouts). Preparing an initial status page message.

product-ops: please include guidance: temporary increased latency and retries may occur; no data loss.

support-liz: drafted status update: "We are investigating increased inference errors and latency in us-west-2. Some requests routed to a degraded availability zone may experience errors or slower responses. Engineers are actively steering traffic and mitigating. More updates shortly." Posting in 5.

netops-tom: AWS says the issue is an AZ-level host networking plane that affects ENIs on a subset of hosts; they are doing host restarts and network path repairs. ETA unknown.

oncall-eng: medium-term mitigation: 1) keep AZ flagged unhealthy 2) spin up additional inference capacity in 2b/2c (prefer dedicated fast-path if available) 3) enable model-variant failover to smaller quantized variant for high latency customers to reduce token CPU/GPU time.

infra-dev: spinning extra instances in 2b/2c now, target +30% capacity for g5 pools. Using `infra-provision --region us-west-2 --az 2b,2c --flavor g5-large --count 8`.

infra-dev: launched 8 instances, joining autoscaling groups. Starting warmup (KV cache priming).

paul: product ops — which customers are impacted most (SLA tiers)? Need list to prioritize handoffs.

product-ops: pulling top-10 by traffic: acct-742, acct-190, acct-33, acct-5. Notifying AMs.

sre-aly: temporary config change suggestion: reduce batch size from 64->32 for request path to lower request queuing on edges. Applying as a hot config on the router.

sre-aly: `router-config set inference.batch_size 32 --scope us-west-2` applied. Expect slightly higher latency but lower tail and fewer 5xxs.

maria: enabling fallback model `rwd-small-quant` for non-SLA traffic. Config: `policy.add failover_model=rwd-small-quant when az_unhealthy=true except tag:enterprise`.

oncall-eng: good. Also enable retry/backoff on client-side: `client-lib` release with exponential jitter is being flagged to edge for retry=2.

support-liz: posted status page update and emailed enterprise contacts. Updating the ticket with mitigation steps.

incident-bot: AWS case 123456789 opened — ongoing.

netops-tom: route53 TTL is 60s for our service record, but we're not changing DNS. Good that we used internal router for immediate steering. Changing DNS would be slower.

product-ops: decision: classify as "partial outage impacting a single AZ". Notify sales + legal for SLA exposure.

oncall-eng: can we give an ETA? With new instances and router steering, we should see error rate drop in ~12-18 minutes as pods warm and traffic shifts.

infra-dev: warmup logs: `warming cache: 0/2000 prefills` then incrementing.

sre-aly: monitoring: 5xx rate now 1.2% and trending down, p95 at 850ms. Good.

support-liz: customers acknowledging the status. A couple flagged immediate rollback requests from a large customer; escalated to product.

product-ops: for the large customer (acct-742) — offer temporary dedicated capacity in 2b while 2a recovers. Engineering OK?

infra-dev: we can allocate dedicated pool in 2b; takes ~20m to spin and attach.

paul: go ahead and provision, liaise with AMs.

maria: note: some long-running sessions lost their KV cache and may get slightly different completions after rebuild. We should monitor quality regression signals.

oncall-eng: agreed, create an eval job for sample prompts from impacted customers to detect regressions.

incident-bot: incident created: incident-2026-1760000000, severity=sev2, owner=oncall-eng.

netops-tom: AWS updates: host remediation progressing, but they warn there may be recurrence as they drain hosts. We'll keep AZ flagged until health checks stable for 30m.

sre-aly: planning handoff in 30m to second oncall. Will prepare notes: what we changed, commands run (`internal-router show-az-health`, `infra-provision` args, `router-config` diff, fallback model policy).

support-liz: scheduled customer follow-ups at 15m and 1h.

product-ops: final note for status: once AWS confirms host state healthy and our health checks stable for 30m, we'll remove AZ degrade flag and gradually shift traffic back with canary control.

oncall-eng: thumbs — continuing to watch.

paul: :thumbsup: great coordination.

maria: leaving logs snippet for postmortem: `ENI-detach: instance i-0abcdef12 detach at 04:09:43Z, reconnection attempts 7, net_err=EPIPE`.

oncall-eng: handoff at 1760003600 to oncall2. All current mitigations documented.

incident-bot: NOTE: create postmortem ticket and attach logs once incident resolved.

support-liz: marking thread resolved for customer comms once error rate <0.2% for 30m.
